findings.problem: println! in the core mapping closure is hidden I/O fused with data construction
findings.failure_mode: logging side-effect corrupts pure data pipeline semantics; output appears on any use of load_shards including in tests, benchmarks, and library consumers with no opt-out
findings.fix: remove println! entirely. Move any logging to the shell layer. The core parsing logic must be pure with no I/O, logging, metrics, or environment access.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing file, permission errors, or unreadable paths
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error that the caller can recover from
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err to convert io::Error into a typed LoadError::Io variant. Signature: pub fn load_shards(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or empty field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input (e.g. 'foo,abc') causes a process abort instead of a typed parse failure on that record
findings.fix: replace with parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue)? after validating the field is non-empty, using u16 directly to avoid lossy casting

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy cast from u32 to u16
findings.failure_mode: values in the range 65536-4294967295 silently truncate to u16 range, corrupting domain data without any error or notification
findings.fix: parse directly as u16: parts[1].trim().parse::<u16>().map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue)? and remove the as u16 cast entirely

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked index access on split result vector
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (empty line or single-field record) panics via index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::MalformedLine)? to split into (_name, value_str) without intermediate Vec, then parse value_str directly. Avoid index, bounds, and get patterns in favor of split_once with typed errors.

findings.problem: I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/collect), allocation (Vec::with_capacity), domain construction (Record), and logging (println!) are all fused in one function with no typed error taxonomy, no try_reserve, no bounded cap, and no pure parsing boundary
findings.failure_mode: the function cannot be unit-tested in isolation, has no allocation failure handling, cannot validate domain caps on record count, and violates the Data/Calculations/Actions architecture required by Holzman
findings.fix: split into: (1) a pure parse_record(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> with no I/O, (2) a bounded load function that validates a max_records cap, uses Vec::new then values.try_reserve(cap).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)?, checks values.len() >= max_records before each push, and handles all I/O errors via Result. ParseError must include MalformedLine, InvalidValue, and EmptyInput variants.

findings.problem: let parts: Vec<String> = line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() creates an intermediate Vec of owned Strings for a two-field CSV record
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation and cloning on every line. For a fixed two-field record this is wasteful and contradicts the Functional Core principle of avoiding intermediate materialization unless required
findings.fix: eliminate the parts vector entirely. Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::MalformedLine)? to get (_name, value_str), then parse value_str directly. This avoids all intermediate allocation for the per-line case.

no profiler data exists showing the hot path or allocation profile
no allocation audit with try_reserve or capacity budget for the Record Vec
no command evidence that cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, or cargo test were executed
no second-ring evidence for any claimed performance characteristics
residual_risk: strict static review only. No commands executed. Seven BLOCKER findings: hidden I/O (println!), two unwrap panic surfaces, lossy u32-to-u16 cast, unchecked indexing, fused shell/domain in a single function, and unnecessary intermediate Vec allocation. The code must be refactored to use typed errors, split_once, direct u16 parsing, and pure core/shell separation before any delivery gate.
